highlights_headline: The upcoming SkiaSharp 4.159.0 release adds experimental image comparison tools and refines texture-edge rendering.
highlights_body: SkiaSharp.Testing provides configurable image acceptance policies and visual difference diagnostics. Ganesh texture sampling and Tizen CPU blur selection change, and Linux x86 native assets are being dropped.

breaking.title: Linux x86 native assets are no longer packaged
breaking.body: Linux x86 native builds and NuGet package entries are removed. Move Linux deployments off x86 before upgrading to this release.

bullets.detail: SkiaSharp.Testing adds SKImageComparison for images, bitmaps and pixmaps, with channel tolerances, masks, mismatch budgets, error metrics and five difference-image styles. Opt in to experimental diagnostic SKIA4001 through NoWarn or a pragma. Results retain no native handles; callers own returned difference images.

Ganesh clamps linear texture sampling slightly inward to avoid reading undefined texels outside subset boundaries. Texture-edge pixels may differ; CPU and Graphite rendering are unaffected by this sampling change.

bullets.lead: Tizen CPU blur configuration takes effect
bullets.detail: Tizen now uses Skia's existing ThreeBoxApprox/Tent CPU blur selection instead of the shader-based Gaussian candidate. Blur pixels and performance may differ; Tizen rendering and performance were not measured in the supporting change.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Restored the Uno Gallery and its view projects to the Windows samples solution.
